# tests/fixtures/protocol-confusions.txt
#
# Every case where a shipped entry reports the service UP against a server
# speaking a DIFFERENT protocol. One "entry peer" pair per line.
#
# tests/network/protocol-confusion.sh compares this against what actually
# happens, in both directions: a pair that appears and is not here fails, and a
# pair here that no longer happens fails too. So the list can only shrink, and
# shrinking it means editing this file on purpose.
#
# --- connect-only entries: the port opening is the whole check, so anything
#     listening satisfies them. Each accepts all 27 other protocols.
ldap ajp13

#
# --- telnet asks only that the server spoke: the banner is the payload, and no
#     fixed text identifies a telnet server. Every peer that speaks first
#     satisfies it.
telnet ftp
telnet imap
telnet imap3
telnet ldap
telnet lpd
telnet netbios-ssn
telnet nntp
telnet pop
telnet pop2
telnet qmqp
telnet qmtp
telnet rsync
telnet smtp
telnet snpp
telnet ssh
telnet submission
telnet svn
telnet vnc
#
# --- the same protocol reached on a different port. Not a defect: an entry
#     cannot distinguish servers that are genuinely identical.
imap imap3
imap3 imap
pop pop2
pop2 pop
smtp submission
submission smtp
#
# --- a real confusion between different protocols. SNPP greets with 220 and
#     answers 221 to a quit, exactly as FTP does, and [ftp] sends nothing
#     FTP-specific in between. Fixable: ask for something only FTP answers.
ftp snpp
